key_insight: A scalable generative "interaction prior" lets high-level intentions (e.g., affordances) produce physically coherent, whole-body human-object interactions without hand-designing low-level motions; balance, contact, and manipulation emerge from the learned prior when coupled with a physics-aware controller.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between abstract intent specification and physically plausible whole-body loco-manipulation by learning priors that generalize across diverse objects, tasks, and contexts, reducing the need for task-specific controllers or manual motion engineering.
method: Train a large-scale generative prior over human-object interaction trajectories that captures balance, contact, and manipulation dynamics.

Represent control hierarchically: high-level affordance/intention conditioning guides the prior, while a physics-aware controller or simulator executes the generated motions to ensure physical plausibility.
Design the system for compositionality so learned priors can be reused and combined to handle new objects, tasks, and environments.
impact: Makes it practical to synthesize generalizable, physically consistent whole-body interactions for humanoid agents and character animation, accelerating development of robust loco-manipulation policies and reducing manual engineering effort.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: high-level intent → InterPrior generative model → physics-aware controller → simulated human-object interaction
Before/After scene grid: manual controller vs. InterPrior output showing improved balance and contact

Task generalization chart: performance or success rate across held-out objects/environments illustrating scalability
paper_title: InterPrior: Scaling Generative Control for Physics-Based Human-Object Interactions
paper_authors: Sirui Xu, Samuel Schulter, Morteza Ziyadi, Xialin He, Xiaohan Fei
